h: Joseph Unites Torah and Good Deeds

p: וַיְבָרֶךְ אֶת יוֹסֵף וַיֹּאמַר הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלְּכוּ אֲבוֹתַי לְפָנָיו וְגוֹמֵר.
— “He blessed Joseph and said: The God before whom my fathers walked,” and so forth.
יָדוּעַ דִּקְדּוּק הַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רכז ב), לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר כָּאן וַיְבָרֶךְ אֶת יוֹסֵף,
— The question raised by the holy Zohar (227b) is well known: why does it say here, “He blessed Joseph”?
דְּלָא אַשְׁכְּחָן הָכָא בְּרָכָה דְּבָרִיךְ לְיוֹסֵף אֶלָּא לִבְנוֹי.
— For here we find a blessing bestowed upon his sons, rather than upon Joseph himself.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 227b: ““He blessed Joseph and said: The God before whom…” This verse requires examination. “He blessed Joseph”—we do not find a blessing here with which he blessed Joseph, but only his sons. If it refers to his sons, it should have said “he blessed them.” What does “he blessed Joseph” mean, when we do not find Joseph being blessed here? Rabbi Yosei said: The word et is precise. It says “et Joseph.” It was a blessing for his sons, and when his sons are blessed, he is blessed, for the blessing of a person’s children is his own blessing. Rabbi Elazar said: “He blessed et Joseph”—et is precise: he blessed the sign of the covenant, the mystery of the covenant that Joseph guarded, because of which he is called righteous. “Et Joseph” means the mystery of the covenant that remained with Joseph. “The God before whom my fathers walked”—“the God” is the mystery of the holy covenant, the holy bond. “My fathers before Him”—precisely “before Him”: they are earlier and higher, preceding this mystery, Abraham and Isaac, for that place is nourished and suckled from them.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Ohr HaChaim, Bereishis 48:15: “‘He blessed Joseph’: we see no blessing for Joseph here. Ramban explained that the blessing of the sons is Joseph's blessing, and so forth. But this does not satisfy the mind, for why should Joseph himself not be blessed in matters that concern him personally? What seems right to me is that with the word ‘He blessed’ Scripture recorded that he blessed Joseph to be blessed always. It may further be explained according to the Sages' statement (Bereishit Rabbah 39:11) that the key of the blessings was in Abraham's hand and he handed it to Isaac, and Isaac handed it to Jacob, and Jacob handed it to Joseph; and this is ‘He blessed’: he placed the key of the blessings in his hand. ‘And he said, The God…’: he began by awakening the love of the ancestors, in the order of the Amidah, which opens with the remembrance of the patriarchs, and he also mentioned his own merit modestly, saying ‘the God who shepherds me,’ for he, Jacob, walked according to His will like a lamb before the shepherd who tends it.”

h: Taste and Fragrance in the Patriarchs

p: וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר בָּזֶה עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרֲכוֹ הַשֵּׁם,
— This may be explained through what we have said about the verse, “Like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed.”
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א׳ קמב ב), דָּא שָׂדֶה דְּתַפּוּחִים, שָׂדֶה דְּאַבָּהָן עִלָּאִין חָמִידֵי לֵיהּ וּמְתַקְּנִין לֵיהּ,
— The holy Zohar (I, 142b) teaches: this is the field of apples, the field that the supernal patriarchs desire and cultivate.
שֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (תַּעֲנִית כט:) דְּרֵיחַ תַּפּוּחִים הַיְינוּ אֶתְרוֹג.
— This accords with Tosafot (Taanit 29b), who explain that the fragrance of apples here refers to the etrog.
וְיָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל) דְּאֶתְרוֹג יֵשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם וָרֵיחַ,
— It is well known that Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 30, describes the etrog as possessing both taste and fragrance.
מְרַמֵּז עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם תּוֹרָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים,
— It alludes to those among Israel who possess both Torah and good deeds.
כִּי בְּחִינַת הָרֵיחַ מִצַּד מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁבַּגּוּף, וְהַטַּעַם מִצַּד הַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ.
— Fragrance corresponds to the good deeds performed by the body, while taste corresponds to the soul within the mind.
וְזֶה כֹּחַ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּ בָּזֶה וְהֶעֱמִידוּ אוּמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית,
— This is the power of our patriarchs, who devoted themselves to this and established the nation of Israel,
לְהַשְׁרִישׁ קְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ לִבְנֵיהֶם אַחֲרֵיהֶם לְעוֹלָם.
— rooting this holiness in their descendants after them forever.
וְזֶה וַיְבָרֶךְ אֶת יוֹסֵף, הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלְּכוּ אֲבוֹתַי לְפָנָיו.
— This is the meaning of “He blessed Joseph: The God before whom my fathers walked.”
וְעַל פִּי דְבָרֵינוּ שֶׁבְּחִינַת הָרֵיחַ, מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים, הוּא הִזְדַּכְּכוּת הַגּוּף בְּפוֹעַל,
— According to our explanation, the aspect of fragrance—good deeds—is the actual refinement of the body,
בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת לִהְיוֹת סוּר מֵרָע וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב, וְהוּא בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף.
— through performing the commandments, turning from evil and doing good; this is Joseph’s aspect.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה כָּל עִנְיָנוֹ וְחֶשְׁקוֹ בְּפֹעַל עֲשֵׂה טוֹב,
— It is known that Abraham our patriarch, peace be upon him, devoted all his concern and desire to actively doing good:
לְהַכְנִיס אוֹרְחִים וּלְקָרְבָם תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה.
— welcoming guests and bringing them beneath the wings of the Divine Presence.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא כח:) אֲנַן מֵאַבְרָהָם נֵיקוּם וְנִיגְמוֹר,
— As it says (Yoma 28b): shall we arise and learn from Abraham?
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַבִּי שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי לִהְיוֹת זְרִיזִין כְּאַבְרָהָם, שֶׁהָיָה זָרִיז מְאֹד בְּפֹעַל עֲשֵׂה טוֹב.
— Rashi explains: to act with Abraham’s alacrity, for he was exceedingly eager in actively doing good.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה זָהִיר מְאֹד לְצַמְצֵם אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּסוּר מֵרָע,
— Likewise Isaac our patriarch, peace be upon him, was exceedingly careful to restrain himself by turning from evil.
שֶׁזֶּה גַּם כֵּן בְּחִינַת מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (קִידּוּשִׁין לט:)
— This too is an aspect of good deeds, as it says (Kiddushin 39b):
יָשַׁב וְלֹא עָבַר עֲבֵירָה נוֹתְנִים לוֹ שָׂכָר כְּעוֹשֶׂה מִצְוָה.
— If one remained inactive and refrained from a transgression, he receives reward as one who performed a commandment.
וְזֶהוּ אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלְּכוּ אֲבוֹתַי לְפָנָיו, דַּיְיקָא אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק שֶׁהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּ בִּבְחִינַת מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים.
— Thus “before whom my fathers walked” refers specifically to Abraham and Isaac, who exerted themselves in the aspect of good deeds.

p: אָמְנָם יַעֲקֹב עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה מְבוֹרָר לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשָׂיו וְעִנְיָנָיו הֵמָּה רַק מִכֹּחוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— Jacob, peace be upon him, however, saw clearly that all his deeds and concerns derived entirely from His blessed power.
וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת טַעֲמֵי תוֹרָה.
— This is the aspect of the inner meanings of Torah.
וְזֶהוּ הָאֱלֹהִים הָרוֹעֶה אוֹתִי מֵעוֹדִי עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה, הַכֹּל רַק מִכֹּחוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— Thus “the God who has shepherded me from my beginning until this day” means that everything derives solely from His blessed power.
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז פְּתִיחַת הַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רכט א) עַל פָּסוּק הַמַּלְאָךְ הַגּוֹאֵל:
— The opening of the holy Zohar’s teaching (229a) on “the angel who redeems” alludes to this:
בַּיִת וָהוֹן נַחֲלַת אָבוֹת, וְכִי נַחֲלַת אָבוֹת אִינְהוּ, וְהָא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא יָהִיב כֹּלָּא לְבַר נָשׁ,
— “House and wealth are an inheritance from fathers.” Are they indeed an inheritance from fathers? Surely the Holy One, blessed be He, gives everything to a person!
אֶלָּא וְכוּלֵי, לְזִמְנִין דְּיַחֲסִין כֹּלָּא לִבְרֵיהּ וִיהֵא אַחְסָנָא דְּאָבוֹת.
— Rather, and so forth, at times a father bequeaths everything to his son, making it an inheritance from the fathers.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי בַיִת מְכוּנֶּה עַל שֵׁם מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים,
— That is, a “house” is a designation for good deeds,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ (סוֹטָה מד.) עַל פָּסוּק אַחַר וּבָנִיתָ בֵיתֶךָ, אֵלּוּ מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים.
— as they expound (Sotah 44a) on “afterward you shall build your house”: these are good deeds.
וְהוֹן מְרַמֵּז עַל טַעֲמֵי תוֹרָה,
— “Wealth” alludes to the inner meanings of Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (עֵירוּבִין סד.) עַל פָּסוּק וְרוֹעֶה זוֹנוֹת יְאַבֶּד הוֹן, מְאַבֵּד הוֹנָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה.
— as it says (Eruvin 64a) regarding “one who keeps company with harlots loses wealth”: he loses the wealth of Torah.
וְכֵן נֶאֱמַר וּבְדַעַת חֲדָרִים יִמָּלְאוּ כָּל הוֹן יָקָר וְנָעִים.
— Likewise it says, “Through knowledge rooms are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.”
וּשְׁתֵּי הַבְּחִינוֹת הֵם שְׁתֵּי נַחֲלוֹת אָבוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
— These two aspects are two inheritances from the patriarchs, as explained above:
כִּי אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק הִתְהַלְּכוּ לְפָנָיו בִּבְחִינַת מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים,
— Abraham and Isaac walked before Him in the aspect of good deeds,
וְיַעֲקֹב עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא בְּחִינַת הוֹנָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה, הָאֱלֹהִים הָרוֹעֶה אוֹתִי כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
— whereas Jacob, peace be upon him, embodies the wealth of Torah: “the God who shepherds me,” as explained above.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 25:1: “But Jacob our father, peace be upon him, who was lowly in his own eyes, as it is said, ‘I am too small for all the kindnesses,’ and it is said, ‘How shall Jacob stand, for he is small?’, brought something new when he said, ‘The God before whom my fathers walked’: that is, they refined themselves through their own exertion, Abraham through the attribute of love and Isaac through the attribute of awe and dread. ‘The God who has shepherded me from my beginning until this day’: of himself he said that he has nothing from his own exertion; only Hashem leads him and shepherds him. Everything is from Hashem, even what one seems to the eye to acquire through exertion, and he has no ‘measure of his own’ at all. Therefore he placed Ephraim before Manasseh, according to the measure of the holiness that Hashem bestows from above, which is far greater than the holiness one seems to acquire through one's toil; and in truth that too is from Hashem.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Chanukah 25 draws the same contrast on this verse between the patriarchs' own exertion and Jacob's recognition that everything comes from God. It adds that this recognition is why Jacob placed Ephraim, holiness given from above, before Manasseh, holiness earned by toil.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach I, Vayechi §3: “But as for me, ‘God who has shepherded me from my beginning until this day’: in every particular action I do, I need Hashem to illuminate my eyes so that I may know His will. Even concerning an action in which I have already seen His will, when it is to be done again I still need to see His will on the second occasion. In truth, in this respect Jacob was the greatest of the Patriarchs, for this is a great spiritual level: that Hashem guides a person continually.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Jacob’s recognition that everything comes from Hashem is expressed here as a continuing practice: each particular action requires renewed receptivity to His will. Even a previous illumination cannot become a self-sufficient possession, sharpening Rav Tzadok’s account of Jacob’s complete dependence on divine power.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 229a: ““The angel who redeems me from all evil, may he bless the lads.” Rabbi Chiyya opened and said: “House and wealth are an inheritance from fathers.” Are they an inheritance from fathers? Does not the Holy One, blessed be He, give everything to a person? Rather, when He grants a person a house and property, the person may bequeath everything to his son, and it becomes an inheritance from fathers. But “a discerning wife is from Hashem,” because when a person receives a wife, he receives her from the Holy One, blessed be He; the Holy One, blessed be He, does not grant her to a person until they proclaim her in heaven.”

— Concerning this he concludes, “May he bless the lads, and may my name be called upon them,”
לְהַנְחִיל לָהֶם לְדוֹרוֹת בְּחִינַת הוֹנוֹ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה.
— bequeathing to them, throughout the generations, the aspect of the wealth of Torah.
וְשֵׁם אֲבוֹתַי אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, הַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים,
— “And the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac” signifies the aspect of good deeds.
וְהוּא כְּלָלוּת בְּחִינַת שָׂדֶה שֶׁל תַּפּוּחִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ בְּחִינַת הַטַּעַם וְהָרֵיחַ,
— Together they encompass the field of apples, which possesses both taste and fragrance,
דְּאַבָּהָן עִלָּאִין חָמִידוּ לֵיהּ וּמְתַקְּנִין לֵיהּ.
— which the supernal patriarchs desire and cultivate.
וּבְרָכָה זוֹ שַׁייָּכָה דַּיְיקָא לְיוֹסֵף כִּדְבָרֵינוּ (וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ב).
— This blessing pertains specifically to Joseph, as we explained (and as discussed in discourse 2).
וְעַל זֶה גָּמַר וְיִדְגּוּ לָרוֹב וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל זֶה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה,
— He therefore concludes, “May they multiply like fish,” and so forth, on which Bereishit Rabbah comments:
מַה דָּגִים וְכוּלֵי כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא טָעֲמוּ טַעַם מַיִם מִיְּמֵיהוֹן,
— Just as fish, and so forth, act as though they had never tasted water in their lives,
כָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל גְּדֵלִים בַּמַּיִם, בַּתּוֹרָה,
— so Israel grow in water—in Torah.
כֵּיוָן שֶׁשּׁוֹמְעִין דָּבָר חָדָשׁ מֵהַתּוֹרָה מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ בְּצִמָּאוֹן וְכוּלֵי,
— As soon as they hear a new Torah teaching, they receive it thirstily, and so forth.
וְהַיְינוּ הַחֶמְדָּה וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה לְהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה,
— This yearning and longing for renewed insight into Torah
הוּא שָׂדֶה דְּאַבָּהָן חָמִידוּ וּמְתַקְּנִין לֵיהּ.
— is the field that the patriarchs desire and cultivate.
